items.name: Proclamation further modifying scope of Canadian products subject to additional (Section 338) duties
items.changes: Adds and removes products from the list of Canadian goods subject to the extra 50% duty.
items.affects: US importers of Canadian valves, carpets, waste products, plywood, paper and machinery.

items.name: Exchange pre-eligibility verification (Working Families Tax Cut Act implementation)
items.changes: Exchanges must verify eligibility before enrollment, and premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions are generally withheld while data matches are unresolved.
items.affects: ACA marketplace enrollees and Exchanges.

items.name: Draft guidance: Action Levels for Cadmium in Processed Food Intended for Babies and Young Children
items.changes: Sets recommended maximum cadmium levels in baby and toddler foods.
items.affects: Baby-food makers and parents.

items.name: Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components (Section 232), Proclamation 11074
items.changes: This corrects the earlier entry: the Oct 22 proclamation finds that wind-turbine imports threaten national security but imposes NO new tariffs or quotas. Commerce and USTR must negotiate with trading partners and report within 180 days (about Apr 20, 2027). Tariffs could follow if talks fail. Existing steel, aluminium and copper Section 232 duties are unchanged.
items.affects: Wind developers and turbine importers (no immediate cost change).

items.name: PIT/CIT tax reform for 2027 (government bill as amended by the Sejm)
items.changes: Superseded. Over constitutional doubts, the Sejm did not vote on the Senate's Oct 27 amendments to this bill, and the government resubmitted the reform as a new bill (R-261105-01), which both chambers have now passed.
items.affects: Same groups as R-261105-01.

items.name: Bill restoring abortion for severe foetal defects; Criminal Code amendment partially decriminalising abortion assistance
items.changes: On Nov 6 the Senate passed both bills without amendments (58–33–3 and 56–34–0). They now await President Nawrocki's signature or veto.
items.affects: Pregnant women, doctors, nurses and midwives, and anyone helping a woman obtain an abortion.

items.name: Draft digital tax on big tech (3% of revenue)
items.changes: Introduces a 3% levy on the Polish revenue of large global tech companies.
items.affects: Large international digital platforms operating in Poland, and possibly Poland–US trade relations.

items.name: Order abolishing six City Hall departments (zarządzenie Prezydenta Miasta Krakowa)
items.changes: Abolishes the departments of Civic Affairs, Kraków Brand, Sustainable Development, Municipal Services, Social Policy and Education, which were a management layer between the mayor and city offices.
items.affects: City Hall staff and directors, and the reporting lines for ZTP, ZDMK, schools and social services.

items.name: Draft fare resolution: return of 20-minute (4 zł) and 40-minute tickets; annual 365 zł ticket for doctoral students
items.changes: Replaces the 15- and 30-minute tickets introduced in March 2026 with 20- and 40-minute tickets, and extends the annual student ticket to doctoral students. The city estimates about 20 million zł a year in lost revenue.
items.affects: All KMK public transport passengers.

items.body: Rada Miasta Krakowa (KO and Nowa Lewica clubs' draft)
items.name: Tourist fee (opłata turystyczna) of 5 zł per night
items.changes: Introduces a fee of 5 zł per night, the statutory maximum, payable when booking accommodation. The first reading took place on 21 October and the final vote is expected in December.
items.affects: Overnight visitors and accommodation providers. Dziennik Polski estimates revenue of up to 50 million zł a year.

items.name: Outbound Investment Security Program regulations (COINS Act implementation)
items.changes: Bans or requires notification of US investments in semiconductor, quantum, supercomputing, hypersonic, 'super intelligence' AI and biotechnology firms tied to China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia; penalties up to IEEPA maximums, including forced divestment.
items.affects: US investors, venture and private-equity funds, and US biotech and tech companies with Chinese partners.

items.name: Order: Requirement for Attestation for All Airline or Other Aircraft Passengers Arriving in the United States (Ebola, DRC)
items.changes: Every international air passenger to or through the US must attest to no presence in DR Congo in the past 21 days; airlines must deny boarding without the attestation.
items.affects: All international air travellers to the US, including from Poland and India, and airlines.

items.body: European Parliament and Council (Directive (EU) 2023/2225, CCD2); Polish implementing act not yet adopted
items.name: Consumer Credit Directive 2 (CCD2)
items.changes: Brings many buy-now-pay-later, interest-free and small loans under full consumer-credit rules. Adds stricter creditworthiness checks, mandatory warnings in credit adverts, rights to human review of automated credit decisions, and longer withdrawal periods where information is missing.
items.affects: Borrowers, payday lenders, BNPL providers, online shops and banks in Poland.

items.name: Act on the tax on extraordinary profits of fuel companies ('Ceny Paliwa Niżej' package)
items.changes: Allows temporary cuts to VAT and excise on fuels and daily maximum retail prices set by the energy minister. Funds this with a 60% tax on fuel companies' profits above their 2025 margin plus 20%, for profits earned 1 March 2026 to 31 March 2027.
items.affects: All drivers and fuel buyers, fuel companies and stations, and the public finances (about 5bn zł).

items.name: Bill amending PIT and CIT (2027 tax reform, resubmitted)
items.changes: Passed by the Sejm on Nov 5 (236–207) and by the Senate on Nov 6 without amendments (63–31–1). It adds a 24% PIT band for income of 130–150k zł and keeps 32% above that, sets 22% CIT for firms with revenue above €50m, raises the solidarity levy to 5% and cuts the lump-sum (ryczałt) limit to €250k. It awaits the President's signature (21 days) and must be published by end-November to apply in 2027.
items.affects: Higher earners, the largest companies and the self-employed on the lump-sum tax.

items.name: Order cutting the residents' monthly network ticket to 90 zł (zarządzenie)
items.changes: The residents' monthly pass for the whole network falls from 99 zł to 90 zł.
items.affects: Kraków residents who buy monthly passes; they save 9 zł a month from Sep 2027.

items.name: Viability Gap Funding scheme for grid-scale energy storage (2026-27 to 2030-31)
items.changes: No change found as of Nov 6: detailed guidelines are still not notified.
items.affects: Power distribution companies, storage developers and battery makers.

items.name: Adjusting Imports of Robotics and Industrial Machinery (Section 232)
items.changes: Finds that robotics and industrial-machinery imports threaten national security, imposes no tariffs yet, and orders negotiations with a status report by Apr 26, 2027.
items.affects: Manufacturers that import industrial robots and machinery, and foreign suppliers (EU and Asia).

items.name: Proclamation establishing the Oval Office National Monument
items.changes: Makes the Oval Office, the Outer Oval Office and the Cabinet Room a national monument under the Antiquities Act. Interior must document, review and consider alternatives before any major alteration or demolition.
items.affects: Future presidents and White House renovation plans.

items.name: 'Rule of law' act on the status of judges appointed on KRS recommendations from 2018 to 2026
items.changes: Voids KRS resolutions from March 2018 to May 2026 that recommended judicial appointments, except those concerning junior judges. The affected posts become vacant and are re-advertised, and the judges concerned return to their earlier posts or professions. The Sejm passed it on Oct 22 and the Senate without amendments on Nov 6 (63–32). It awaits the President.
items.affects: Judges appointed since 2018 on the recommendation of the reformed KRS, courts and litigants.

items.name: Anti-alcohol law: night sales ban (22:00–06:00) and alcohol advertising ban
items.changes: Bans retail alcohol sales from 22:00 to 06:00, except in restaurants and bars, and lets municipalities widen the ban. It also bans alcohol advertising and promotions such as discounts, bundles and loyalty schemes. Senate committees proposed moving the start to June 1, 2027, banning home delivery of online orders and allowing limited ads for non-alcoholic beer. If the full Senate adopts the amendments, the bill returns to the Sejm. (Start date: 1 June 2027 in the Senate committees' version; the Sejm version said 1 January 2027.)
items.affects: Shops, petrol stations, the alcohol and advertising industries, and consumers.

items.name: Limits on doctors' pay and working time
items.changes: The Senate amended it on Nov 6 (61–32–2): minimum employment raised to a quarter of a full-time post, and the NFZ work ban for doctors who certify falsehoods dropped. It returns to the Sejm.
items.affects: Doctors working in publicly funded healthcare, and hospitals.

items.name: Draft resolution freezing Clean Transport Zone (SCT) entry fees for 2027-2028
items.changes: Keeps SCT entry fees at 100 zł a month, 2.50 zł an hour or 5 zł a day through 2027-2028, instead of the scheduled rise to 250 zł a month in 2027 and 500 zł in 2028. Zone area, emission rules and exemptions stay the same.
items.affects: Drivers of non-compliant cars entering the SCT, and Kraków residents who pay for entry

items.name: Agnipath scheme: two-year 'Second Tour of Duty' for Agniveers
items.changes: Agniveers not absorbed after four years (about 75% of a batch) may opt to serve two more years, for six in total, and then apply for regular enrolment under objective selection criteria. The 25% merit-based absorption at four years continues.
items.affects: The first Agniveer batch (exit due Nov 21) and all later batches in the Army, Navy and Air Force. Pay and Seva Nidhi terms for the extra years are not yet published.

items.name: Trade Margin Rationalisation for 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines (30% cap)
items.changes: Wholesalers and retailers can add at most 30% on top of the price to distributor for 137 cancer drugs that are not under price control. Companies had to cut printed MRPs to comply.
items.affects: Cancer patients and families buying these drugs, pharmacies and drug makers. The government says some brands could fall by up to 70%.

items.name: Amendment to the nuclear special act (act on preparing and carrying out nuclear power investments)
items.changes: Site decisions for nuclear plants would no longer expire after 10 years; the investor would get land rights automatically once the site decision is final; some documents could be filed in English; PEJ’s yearly public-funding caps are reshuffled (2026 down to 8bn zł, 2030 up to 9.6bn zł).
items.affects: Polskie Elektrownie Jądrowe and the first nuclear plant project in Pomerania, landowners near the site, and the nuclear regulator (PAA).

items.body: General Assembly of Constitutional Tribunal judges
items.name: Resolution amending the Constitutional Tribunal’s Rules of Procedure
items.changes: The Tribunal president can approve the budget report only after a positive opinion from all judges; judges’ meetings outside the Assembly count for informing judges. Takes effect the day after publication.
items.affects: How the Constitutional Tribunal is run, and the power of its president, Bogdan Święczkowski.

items.name: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2487 on AI regulatory sandboxes
items.changes: Sets common EU-wide rules for how national AI regulatory sandboxes are set up, run and supervised under the AI Act, so they do not differ country to country.
items.affects: AI developers and start-ups testing products under regulator supervision, and Poland’s AI Act authorities.

items.name: Amendment to the Act on providing services by electronic means: procedure for orders blocking illegal online content (second DSA-implementing law)
items.changes: Creates a fast procedure for orders that restrict access to illegal content online. Blocking needs court approval, except for some categories such as sexual content involving children. Vetoed by the President on 13 Nov 2026.
items.affects: Online platforms and internet users in Poland. It also completes Poland's implementation of the EU Digital Services Act, which could otherwise bring EU penalties.

items.body: MeitY / Data Protection Board of India
items.name: DPDP Rules 2025 – Rule 4 and First Schedule (consent managers)
items.changes: Consent managers, the platforms through which people give, manage and withdraw consent to data use, can now register with the Data Protection Board under set conditions and obligations.
items.affects: Consent-manager platforms, and later all data fiduciaries that integrate with them (most company duties start May 13, 2027).

items.name: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility (NPRM, Docket USCIS-2026-0529)
items.changes: Removes the rule that tells officers to defer to an earlier approval when extending a worker petition for the same person and facts.
items.affects: H-1B and other I-129 workers and their employers seeking extensions, including many Indian professionals. DHS expects more evidence requests and slower processing.

items.name: Act amending certain acts for patriotic education (print 671)
items.changes: Schools must take every pupil at least once on a trip to memorial, heritage or military sites, and secondary schools must run engineering clubs.
items.affects: Schools, pupils and local governments that run schools

items.name: Amendment to the act on anti-terrorist activities (print 2870)
items.changes: Creates a standing 'special event' security regime for big events: security plans, police data processing and vetting of staff.
items.affects: Event organisers, police, ABW, voivodes, people working at such events

items.name: Draft regulation exempting donations to victims of the 7 Nov 2026 Kraków attack from inheritance and gift tax
items.changes: Gifts made from 7 Nov 2026 to 31 Dec 2027 to the injured and to families of those killed would be tax-free.
items.affects: Victims, their families and donors

items.name: Notification under the IFSCA Act, 2019 declaring 'commodity trading contract' a financial product
items.changes: Commodity trading contracts by units at GIFT City become a regulated financial product.
items.affects: Commodity traders and trade-finance firms considering GIFT City

items.name: UAPA notification extending the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation
items.changes: Keeps the IRF an unlawful association for five more years.
items.affects: IRF and its affiliates
